title: Float keys below the smallest double are different keys when their values differ
notes: `1e-400` and `2e-400` stand for 10^-400 and 2*10^-400. A double rounds both to zero; the kit compares keys by exact decimal value (see the overflow case with different values), so they are two keys. The tag `convention` marks the choice of exact value over the double that the specification leaves open (YAML 1.2.2 section 10.2.1.4 says a float is an approximation whose range and accuracy depend on the implementation, and section 3.2.1.3 compares scalars by canonical form.). A library may instead refuse the document with a `limit` error; it must not call the keys duplicates. A patch is used because 0.0 is not the value of either key.

provenance.reference: A key identity taken from the rounded double, so two keys that round to zero were refused as duplicates.
